candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Genesis
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis VIII.21 (NPNF S2 V13). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Genesis (c. 362 AD)

After Noah's post-flood sacrifice — 'the LORD smelled a sweet savour; and the LORD said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man's sake' — Ephrem reads as the inauguration of the Noahic covenant of cosmic stability. The 'sweet savour' (the Syriac rīhā d-nyahha) Ephrem takes as the prototype of every subsequent acceptable sacrifice — Abel's, Abraham's, the Mosaic sacrificial system, and ultimately the eucharistic sacrifice of Christ. God's interior speech ('said in his heart') Ephrem takes as decisive: the divine commitment is irrevocable not because of external pressure but because of intrinsic divine resolve. The Tewahedo liturgical reading of this verse on Noah's feast day (10th of Magabit) preserves this Ephremic emphasis on the interior divine commitment.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Genesis. Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.
